## Default Context

This repo contains multiple packages, but **`packages/coding-agent/`** is the primary focus. Unless otherwise specified, assume work refers to this package.

**Terminology**: When the architect says "agent" or asks "why is agent doing X", they mean the **coding-agent package implementation**, not you (the assistant). The coding-agent is a CLI tool — questions about its behavior refer to code in `packages/coding-agent/`, not your current session.

### Package Structure

| Package                 | Description                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/ai`           | Multi-provider LLM client with streaming support                                        |
| `packages/catalog`      | Model catalog: bundled models.json, provider descriptors, model identity/classification |
| `packages/agent`        | Agent runtime with tool calling and state management                                    |
| `packages/coding-agent` | Main CLI application (primary focus)                                                    |
| `packages/tui`          | Terminal UI library with differential rendering                                         |
| `packages/natives`      | Bindings for native text/image/grep operations                                          |
| `packages/stats`        | Local observability dashboard (`tau stats`)                                             |
| `packages/tautype`      | ArkType-compatible schema validation with a lazy JIT runtime                            |
| `packages/utils`        | Shared utilities (logger, streams, temp files)                                          |
| `crates/tau-natives`     | Rust crate for performance-critical text/grep ops                                       |

**Catalog import convention**: code in this repo imports catalog _values_ (bundled models, model-thinking helpers, identity, descriptors, model manager/cache) from `@tau/tau-catalog/<module>` — never via `@tau/tau-ai`. The tau-ai barrel re-exports only the model/effort _types_ its own signatures use (`Model`, `Api`, `ThinkingConfig`, `Effort`, …); type-only imports of those from `@tau/tau-ai` are fine.

## GitHub

- Before posting a GitHub comment or creating an issue, MUST show the target and proposed text and obtain user confirmation. An explicit instruction to post supplied text to a specified target already counts as confirmation.
- A request to address or fix PR feedback permits drafting replies, not posting them without confirmation. A request only to get or check comments is read-only.
- When authorized to resolve review feedback, MUST verify the fix, obtain approval for a factual reply citing the change and verification, and post it in the existing thread before resolving. NEVER resolve if the reply is unapproved or posting fails.
- Permission to work on a PR does not authorize unrelated comments or issue creation.

### Pull requests

When authorized to create or edit a contributor-submitted PR, follow the checklist below. RoboOMP-managed PRs follow their dedicated workflow and enforced body format in `python/robtau/src/prompts/system_append.md` instead.

- MUST read `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` first. Preserve the template sections and checklist, including when shortening an existing description.
- MUST obtain at least one sentence written by the contributor in their own words explaining what changed and why, as required by `CONTRIBUTING.md`. If it is missing, ask the contributor; NEVER generate a substitute. Preserve that sentence during edits.
- For user-facing changes, MUST follow the [Changelog](#changelog) attribution rules. Internal issue fixes keep their issue links. For external contributions, add the PR link and contributor credit after GitHub assigns the number, then push the entry before marking the changelog checklist item complete.
- MUST read back the published PR description after creating or editing it. Check only verified checklist items; explain skipped or inapplicable checks in `Testing`.

## Code Quality

- No `any` unless absolutely necessary.
- **NEVER use `ReturnType<>`** — use the actual type name.
- **NEVER use inline imports** — no `await import()`, no `import("pkg").Type` in type positions, no dynamic type imports. Always top-level.
- Check `node_modules` for external API types instead of guessing.
- **Barrel exports**: prefer `export * from "./module"` over named re-exports, including `export type { ... } from`. In pure `index.ts` barrels, use star re-exports even for single-specifier cases. If stars create ambiguity, remove the redundant export path; do not keep duplicates.
- **Class privacy**: use ES `#private` fields; leave externally accessible members bare. **No `private`/`protected`/`public` keyword on fields or methods**, except on **constructor parameter properties** where TypeScript requires it (e.g. `constructor(private readonly session: ToolSession)`).
- **Promises**: use `Promise.withResolvers()` instead of `new Promise((resolve, reject) => ...)`.
- **Prompts**: never build prompts in code (no inline strings, template literals, or concatenation). Prompts live in static `.md` files; use Handlebars for dynamic content. Import them via `import content from "./prompt.md" with { type: "text" }` — not `readFile`.
- **Worker scripts**: workers re-enter the CLI entrypoint; never spawn separate worker entry modules. `cli.ts` declares itself as the worker host at startup (`declareWorkerHostEntry()` from `@tau/tau-utils/env`) and dispatches hidden argv selectors (`__tau_worker_stats_sync`, `__tau_worker_tab`, `__tau_worker_js_eval`, `__tau_worker_tiny_inference`) before loading the command registry. Spawn sites use:
  ```ts
  import { workerHostEntry } from "@tau/tau-utils";
  const hostEntry = workerHostEntry();
  const worker = hostEntry
  	? new Worker(hostEntry, { type: "module", argv: ["__tau_worker_<name>"] })
  	: new Worker(new URL("./<worker>.ts", import.meta.url).href, { type: "module" });
  ```
  When the process was started from the tau CLI — source `cli.ts`, npm-bundle `dist/cli.js`, or compiled binary — `workerHostEntry()` is `Bun.main` and the worker re-enters the single entry module, so no per-worker `--compile` entrypoints or bundle entries exist. Outside a CLI host (`bun test`, SDK embedding, standalone `tau-stats`) it returns `null` and the direct-module fallback loads the worker source. New worker kinds MUST add their selector to the dispatch table in `cli.ts` and keep the fallback branch.
  History: `with { type: "file" }` only copied the entry as a raw asset (workers crashed silently in compiled binaries — issues #1011, #1027), and the later literal-path + extra-entrypoint pattern required keeping spawn literals and two build scripts in sync (issue #1150). The smoke probe below is the live validation of this contract.
  Validate any new worker with the dedicated smoke probe: `tau --smoke-test` spawns the stats sync worker and the tiny-model subprocess, pings them, and exits — it's wired into `ci:test:smoke` and `scripts/install-tests/run-ci.sh` so binary, source-link, and tarball installs all exercise it. Add a sibling smoke if the new worker is on a different module graph.

## Central Utilities

Before writing a helper, check whether one already exists — `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/`, `@tau/tau-utils`, `@tau/tau-tui`, and the domain modules next to your callsite. This applies to **everything**: VCS wrappers, formatting/truncation/path-display helpers, image handling, clipboard, streams, temp files, caching. The central versions carry hardening a fresh copy always loses (timeouts, output caps, non-interactive env, lock avoidance, caching, TUI sanitization).

- Search first: `grep` for the operation before implementing it. Two implementations of the same thing is a bug even when both work.
- Examples of the pattern: `@tau/tau-natives/vcs` and `src/utils/active-repo-context.ts` are the only sanctioned way to run git/jj (`import * as vcs from "@tau/tau-natives/vcs"` — never hand-spawn via `$`/`Bun.spawn`); rendering goes through the helpers in TUI Sanitization below (`replaceTabs`, `truncateToWidth`, `shortenPath`, `PREVIEW_LIMITS`) rather than ad-hoc string math.
- Missing capability? Extend the central helper (new option, new sub-function on the namespace) and call it — don't fork its logic locally.

## Bun Over Node

Use Bun APIs where they provide a cleaner alternative; fall back to `node:*` only for what Bun doesn't cover. **Never spawn shell commands for operations with proper APIs** (e.g., don't `Bun.spawnSync(["mkdir", "-p", dir])` — use `mkdirSync`).

### Quick reference

| Operation       | Use                                       | Not                                |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| File read/write | `Bun.file()`, `Bun.write()`               | `readFileSync`, `writeFileSync`    |
| Spawn process   | `` $`cmd` ``, `Bun.spawn()`               | `child_process`                    |
| Sleep           | `Bun.sleep(ms)`                           | `setTimeout` promise               |
| Binary lookup   | `$which("git")` from `@tau/tau-utils` | `spawnSync(["which", "git"])`      |
| HTTP server     | `Bun.serve()`                             | `http.createServer()`              |
| SQLite          | `bun:sqlite`                              | `better-sqlite3`                   |
| Hashing         | `Bun.hash()`, `Bun.password.*`, WebCrypto | `node:crypto`                      |
| Path resolution | `import.meta.dir`, `import.meta.path`     | `fileURLToPath` dance              |
| JSON5           | `Bun.JSON5.parse()` / `.stringify()`      | `json5` package                    |
| JSONL           | `Bun.JSONL.parse()` / `.parseChunk()`     | `text.split("\n").map(JSON.parse)` |
| String width    | `Bun.stringWidth()`                       | `get-east-asian-width`, custom     |
| Text wrapping   | `Bun.wrapAnsi()`                          | custom ANSI-aware wrappers         |

### Process execution

Prefer Bun Shell (`` $`cmd` ``) for simple commands:

```typescript
import { $ } from "bun";

const result = await $`git status`.cwd(dir).quiet().nothrow();
if (result.exitCode === 0) {
	const text = result.text();
}

$`do-stuff ${tmpFile}`.quiet().nothrow(); // fire and forget
```

Methods: `.quiet()`, `.nothrow()`, `.text()`, `.cwd(path)`.

Use `Bun.spawn`/`Bun.spawnSync` only for: long-running processes (LSP, kernels), streaming stdin/stdout/stderr (SSE, JSON-RPC), or process control (signals, kill, complex lifecycle).

When using `pipe` mode, cast the stream:

```typescript
const child = Bun.spawn(["cmd"], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
const reader = (child.stdout as ReadableStream<Uint8Array>).getReader();
```

### Node module imports

Always use **namespace imports** for `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:os`:

```typescript
import * as fs from "node:fs/promises";
import * as path from "node:path";
import * as os from "node:os";
```

- Async-only file → `node:fs/promises`.
- Needs both sync and async → `node:fs`, then `fs.promises.xxx` for async.

### File I/O

Prefer Bun:

```typescript
const text = await Bun.file(path).text();
const data = await Bun.file(path).json();
await Bun.write(path, data); // auto-creates parent dirs
```

Use `node:fs/promises` for directory ops (`fs.mkdir`, `fs.rm`, `fs.readdir`) — Bun has no native directory APIs. Avoid sync APIs in async flows; use sync only when forced by a synchronous interface.

**Anti-patterns:**

- `existsSync`/`readFileSync`/`writeFileSync` in async code → `Bun.file()` APIs.
- `mkdir(dirname(path), …)` before `Bun.write(path, …)` → redundant; `Bun.write` handles it.
- `if (await file.exists()) { await file.json() }` → two syscalls plus race. Use try-catch with `isEnoent`:
  ```typescript
  import { isEnoent } from "@tau/tau-utils";
  try {
  	return await Bun.file(path).json();
  } catch (err) {
  	if (isEnoent(err)) return null;
  	throw err;
  }
  ```
- Multiple `Bun.file(path)` handles for the same path (including across `checkX`/`loadX` helpers).
- `Buffer.from(await Bun.file(x).arrayBuffer())` → `await fs.readFile(path)`.
- Existence check + try-catch around the same read → drop the existence check.

### Streams

Prefer centralized helpers:

```typescript
import { readStream, readLines } from "./utils/stream";
const text = await readStream(child.stdout);
for await (const line of readLines(stream)) {
	/* ... */
}
```

Manual reader loops only when the protocol requires it (SSE, streaming JSON-RPC).

### Misc

- **Sleep**: `await Bun.sleep(ms)`, never `new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms))`.
- **Password hashing**: `Bun.password.hash(pw, "bcrypt")` / `Bun.password.verify(pw, hash)`.
- **String width**: `Bun.stringWidth(text, { countAnsiEscapeCodes?: false })`.
- **Wrapping**: `Bun.wrapAnsi(text, width, { wordWrap, hard, trim })`.

## Model/Provider Policy Lives in KDL

**NEVER hard-code model- or provider-conditional policy in TypeScript.** No `id.includes("claude")`, no model-name regexes, no per-model lookup tables (effort ladders, pricing, context windows, modalities, API routing, quirk flags). All of it belongs in the KDL rule tree at `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/`, compiled by `bun run gen:compat` into the committed `rules.json` and resolved at build time via `resolveModelPolicy`/`buildModel`.

Ownership strata (see `src/compat/rules/README.md`):

- `taxonomy/*.kdl` — identity: class membership, families, revision extraction, reviewed overrides, suffix collapse.
- `classes/*.kdl` — model-lineage truths (behavior inherent to a model line, on any host).
- `providers/*.kdl` — deployment contracts (behavior a host imposes), plus documented exact-id residue.
- `runtime/behavior.kdl` — heuristics that run before/outside exact model lookup (`api-routes`, `model-limits`, `exclude-models`, `pricing-peer`, hosted defaults).

Rules for TS code:

- Branching on model identity in TS is allowed **only** through structured facts from `classifyModel()` (`class`/`family`/`revision`/effort facts) — never through string matching on ids, and prefer a KDL axis when one can express the policy.
- Discovery mappers map authoritative upstream fields as reported; seed neutral values only for fields the upstream omits or misreports **and** KDL explicitly owns via a correction axis (`input-modalities`, `cost-patch`, `limits-patch`, `context-window-floor`, thinking axes). Assert rule-owned corrections through `buildModel`; raw discovery specs remain the right assertion surface for parsing/normalization contracts.
- An id that no selector can isolate gets an exact-id `models` residue rule with a comment — never a special case in TS.
- Equal-rank rule overlaps throw `AmbiguousOverlapError` at resolve time; fix with an explicit `priority=` in KDL, not code.
- After editing rules: `bun run gen:compat` and commit `rules.json` alongside the `.kdl` change.

## Generated Files

**NEVER edit `packages/catalog/src/models.json` directly.** It is generated from upstream sources (stencil.so, provider catalog discovery, OpenCode docs) by `packages/catalog/scripts/generate-models.ts` and the descriptors/resolvers in `packages/catalog/src/provider-models/`. Hand-edits get overwritten on the next regen. The same applies to `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules.json`, compiled from the KDL tree by `bun run gen:compat`.

To change an entry, fix the source:

- **Model/provider policy** (identity, thinking ladders, wire quirks, modality/limit/pricing corrections, API routing, roster exclusions) → the KDL tree in `packages/catalog/src/compat/rules/` (see the section above).
- **Provider catalog entries** (default model, discovery factory/flags) → the `CATALOG_PROVIDERS` table in `packages/catalog/src/provider-models/descriptors.ts`.
- **Discovery/request plumbing** (endpoint shapes, auth, response parsing) → the mappers in `packages/catalog/src/provider-models/openai-compat.ts`.
- **Generator wiring** (upstream merges, premium multipliers, post-processing order) → `packages/catalog/scripts/generate-models.ts`.

Regenerate with `bun run gen:compat` and/or `bun run gen:models` and commit the generated files alongside the source change. Add a regression test against the **rule/descriptor/mapper**, not the bundled JSON, so it survives upstream metadata shifts.

## Logging and CLI Output

Code that may run while the TUI, RPC, SDK, workers, or background runtimes are active MUST NOT use `console.log`/`error`/`warn`; it corrupts rendering or protocols. Use the centralized logger:

```typescript
import { logger } from "@tau/tau-utils";

logger.error("MCP request failed", { url, method });
logger.warn("Theme file invalid, using fallback", { path });
logger.debug("LSP fallback triggered", { reason });
```

Logs go to `~/.tau/logs/tau.YYYY-MM-DD.log` with automatic rotation. Standalone CLI commands that exit without entering the TUI MAY use `console.*` or process streams for intentional user-facing output. Keep structured stdout clean. This exception is semantic, not filename-based; shared code must use `logger` or an explicit output sink.

## TUI Sanitization

All text displayed in tool renderers must be sanitized. Raw content (file contents, error messages, tool output) breaks terminal rendering: tabs → visual holes, long lines → overflow, paths → leak home directory.

**Rules:**

- **Tabs → spaces** via `replaceTabs()` (from `@tau/tau-tui` or `../tools/render-utils`).
- **Truncate** lines with `truncateToWidth()` / `ui.truncate()`. Use `TRUNCATE_LENGTHS` constants.
- **Shorten paths** with `shortenPath()` (replaces home with `~`).
- **Preview limits** from `PREVIEW_LIMITS`. No ad-hoc numbers.

**Apply to every render path**, not just the happy one:

- Success output (file previews, command output, search results).
- **Error messages** — these often embed file content (e.g., patch failure messages include unmatched lines). If a message contains file content, it needs `replaceTabs()`.
- Diff content (added and removed).
- Streaming previews.

### Streaming tool previews

Tool-call previews can have **multiple render paths**. If you add preview-only fields or depend on partially streamed args, update every path — not only the final renderer. Streamed argument buffers decode into display args via `decodeStreamedToolArgs` / `ToolArgsRevealController` (`modes/controllers/tool-args-reveal.ts`); both the live event path and transcript rebuilds must go through them — never spread provider-parsed `arguments` next to a raw `__partialJson` (parsed args lag the stream by a throttled parse window).

For the bash tool specifically:

- The pending preview may need raw `partialJson`, not just parsed `arguments`. Parsed args lag until a JSON object closes, which makes inline env assignments appear only at the end.
- Preserve preview-only fields (e.g. `__partialJson`) through `event-controller.ts`, transcript rebuilds in `ui-helpers.ts`, and merged call/result rendering in `tool-execution.ts`. Missing one path causes inconsistent previews.
- `ToolExecutionComponent.#buildRenderContext()` for bash must work even before a result exists — the renderer uses call args plus render context to show the command preview while streaming.
- Verify both live streaming and rebuilt transcript paths after any bash preview change. A fix in one path does not fix the other.

## Commands

- NEVER commit unless asked.
- Never use `tsc`/`npx tsc` — always `bun check`.
- Never run `cargo test` directly for Rust tests — use `bun run test:rs`. It runs `cargo nextest run` (config: `.config/nextest.toml`) followed by a `cargo test --doc` pass, because nextest does not execute doctests. The doctest pass currently executes nothing (tau-natives is a `cdylib`, which rustdoc skips; tau-builtins' examples are `ignore`d vendored uutils docs) and exists so the first runnable doctest added to a lib crate is actually run.
- Merge commits (maintainer merges of PRs) follow: `Merge PR #<number>: <conventional PR subject> (@<author>)` — e.g. `Merge PR #6386: feat(catalog): add native Meta Model API provider (@eggpeat)`.
## Rust Build Profiles

Profiles live in the root `Cargo.toml`; `.cargo/config.toml` carries the settings Cargo.toml cannot express. Both are committed, so no local `~/.cargo/config.toml` is required.

| Profile | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `dev` | Default. Line tables for our crates, no debuginfo for deps, deps at `opt-level = 2`. |
| `release` | Shipping build: fat LTO, 1 codegen unit, stripped. |
| `local` | Fast local release iteration: thin LTO, 16 codegen units, incremental. |
| `profiling` | `release` codegen with symbols kept, for `perf`/`samply`/Instruments. |
| `ci` | Thin LTO, no debuginfo, stripped. |

**Never set `split-debuginfo = "off"` on a profile that has debuginfo.** On Mach-O the linker never merges DWARF into the executable — it writes a debug map (`N_OSO`) pointing at the `.o` files, and `"unpacked"` is what keeps those files. With `"off"` every backtrace frame in our own crates silently loses `file:line`; the `panicked at foo.rs:3` header still prints (that is `#[track_caller]`, not debuginfo), which makes the loss easy to miss. `ci` may use `"off"` only because it sets `debug = false`.

`embed-metadata = false` (in `.cargo/config.toml`) keeps crate metadata in `.rmeta` instead of duplicating it into every rlib — measured 196 MB → 130 MB on a reqwest-sized graph at identical build times. Its accepted spelling is toolchain-coupled; keep it in sync with `rust-toolchain.toml`.

Rejected, with measurements, so nobody re-litigates them: **sccache** (cannot cache incremental, bin, or proc-macro crates — measured slower than not using it), **mold** (ELF-only; no Mach-O support), and **`panic = "abort"` on `dev`** (Cargo ignores `panic` for the test profile, so the whole dep graph builds twice — 131 MB → 214 MB).

## Testing Guidance

Test the contract the system exposes — not the easiest internal detail to assert.

- Every new test must defend one **concrete, externally observable contract**: behavior, output shape, state transition, error mapping, or a regression-prone parsing boundary. If you cannot name the contract, do not add the test.

### Good vs. bad test filter

- **Name the failure mode.** Every test MUST state what a consumer observes if it regresses. Cannot name one? NEVER add it.
- **Good: transformation.** One fixture MAY prove parse/render/normalize/encode/resolve behavior when output is computed, not echoed.
- **Good: branch or boundary.** Distinct inputs, empty values, malformed input, version/provider routing, and state transitions MUST prove distinct outcomes.
- **Good: external contract.** Exact bytes/shape MAY be asserted when a provider, parser, protocol, or persisted consumer reads them.
- **Good: precedence or negative contract.** Keep explicit `false`/override-wins assertions and required absence only when they prevent a documented leak, downgrade, 400, or incompatible wire field.
- **Good: regression.** A repro MUST trigger the prior real failure path and assert the corrected observable result.
- **Bad: static echo.** NEVER test a constructor/builder merely copied a fixture or baked constant into an in-memory config/metadata field.
- **Bad: success passthrough.** NEVER assert `fn(x) === x` when `x` was already supplied/declared valid; assert a transform, rejection, or downstream effect instead.
- **Bad: wording/defaults.** NEVER assert prompt/UI boilerplate, a default literal, object existence, non-empty output, or length growth without a consumer contract.
- **Bad: duplicate rows.** Parameterized/loop rows MUST each cover a distinct branch, provider/model path, or consumer contract; delete same-path duplicates.
- **Metadata exception.** Exact metadata, identity, ordering, or `undefined` MAY remain only when a downstream consumer depends on it and the test establishes branch, precedence, negative-contract, wire, or regression evidence.
- **Termination exception.** For cyclic/large inputs, assert a bounded output, surfaced error, or state change; bare `not.toThrow()` is insufficient.
- No placeholder tests, tautologies, or "the code ran" assertions (`expect(true).toBe(true)`, bare `not.toThrow()`, non-empty string checks, length-grew checks, "prompt exists" checks without semantic assertion).
- Prefer contract-level tests over implementation details. Avoid asserting internal helper wiring, field assignment, singleton identity, incidental ordering, prompt boilerplate, or passthrough option forwarding unless another component depends on that exact detail.
- Don't duplicate coverage across abstraction levels. If an integration test already proves the behavior, drop the narrower unit test that restates it through mocks.
- Tests **must be full-suite safe**, not just file-local safe. No long-lived file-wide mutations of `Bun.*`, `process.platform`, `process.env`, or `Bun.env` when a narrower seam exists. Prefer per-test `vi.spyOn(...)` with `vi.restoreAllMocks()` in `afterEach`. A test that passes alone but poisons later files is broken.
- **Never use `mock.module()`**. Bun's `mock.module()` mutates the global module registry and leaks across files ([oven-sh/bun#12823](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/12823)). Use `spyOn` on the imported module object instead. For pass deps, import the pass and spy on `.run`. For package deps, namespace-import and spy on the exported function.
- For lifecycle/stateful code, prefer one test per invariant or transition over several tiny tests asserting one field each from the same transition.
- For error handling, trigger the real failure path and assert the surfaced contract — don't instantiate error classes directly or inspect internal metadata.
- Smoke tests are acceptable only when they catch a failure mode narrower tests would miss. "Package boots" or "command starts" alone is not enough.
- Assert exact strings, ordering, and formatting only when downstream code parses or depends on the exact bytes. Otherwise assert semantic content.
- Compile-time guarantees → type checks/type tests, not runtime placeholders.
- **Never source-grep.** A test that reads an implementation file (`.ts`/`.rs`/build script) and asserts on its _text_ — `expect(src).toContain("someCall()")`, `.toMatch(/import .../)`, `.not.toContain("oldName")`, or "comment must say X" — is banned. It tests how code _looks_, not what it _does_: it breaks on harmless refactors (comment reflow, rename, import reorder) and passes while the behavior is broken. Assert the observable contract instead (run the code, check output/state/error), use the runtime smoke probe for wiring you cannot exercise in-process, and enforce structural invariants (no value-import of X, no self-import) with a type test or an oxlint rule — never a string scan of the source. (Reading a file your code _wrote_ — apply-patch result, generated bundle, temp fixture — and asserting on that output is fine; that is behavior, not a source grep.)
- Don't add tests for tiny low-risk changes unless they protect a real contract or fix a regression-prone edge case.
- Prefer focused package-local verification for the changed area.

## Changelog

Location: `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` (per package).

**NEVER update changelogs unless explicitly asked.** Do not add, edit, or reorder entries as part of a feature, fix, or PR unless the architect requests it.

**Format** — sections under `## [Unreleased]`:

- `### Breaking Changes` (first if present)
- `### Added`
- `### Changed`
- `### Fixed`
- `### Removed`

**Rules:**

- New entries always go under `## [Unreleased]`.
- Entries are one line, brief, and user-facing: lead with what the architect will see or can now do. Root-cause narration and implementation detail belong in the commit/PR, not the changelog.
- Never modify already-released sections (e.g., `## [0.12.2]`) — they are immutable.
- Don't flag changelog section order or formatting in reviews or PRs — `bun run release` runs `fix-changelogs` which normalizes everything automatically.

**Attribution:**

- Internal (from issues): `Fixed foo bar ([#123](https://github.com/toxicwind/tau/issues/123))`.
- External contributions: `Added feature X ([#456](https://github.com/toxicwind/tau/pull/456) by [@username](https://github.com/username))`.

## Releasing

1. Ensure all changes since last release are in each affected package's `[Unreleased]` section.
2. Run `bun run release`.

The script handles version bump, CHANGELOG finalization, commit, tag, publish, and adding new `[Unreleased]` sections.

43: 	/** Tags applied to every retain — non-empty in per-project-tagged mode. */
44: 	retainTags?: string[];
45: 	/** Tag filter applied to every recall/reflect — non-empty in per-project-tagged mode. */
46: 	recallTags?: string[];
47: 	recallTagsMatch?: "any" | "all" | "any_strict" | "all_strict";
48: 	config: HindsightConfig;
49: 	session: AgentSession;
50: 	banksSet: Set<string>;
51: 	lastRetainedTurn?: number;
52: 	hasRecalledForFirstTurn?: boolean;
53: 	/**
54: 	 * When set, this entry is a subagent alias that reuses the parent's bank,
55: 	 * scope, config, client, and banksSet. Aliases skip auto-recall and
56: 	 * auto-retain — those run on the parent only — but the recall/retain/reflect
57: 	 * tools resolve via the alias so they persist to the same bank as the parent.
58: 	 */
59: 	aliasOf?: HindsightSessionState;
60: }
61: 
62: /**
63:  * Debounced batch queue for tool-initiated `retain` calls owned by one
64:  * Hindsight session state instance.
65:  *
66:  * Auto-retain (`HindsightSessionState.retainSession`) is intentionally not
67:  * routed through this queue — it submits a full transcript as one large item
68:  * and already runs `async: true` server-side.
69:  */
70: export class HindsightRetainQueue {
71: 	readonly #state: HindsightSessionState;
72: 	#items: PendingRetainItem[] = [];
73: 	#timer?: NodeJS.Timeout;
74: 	#flushing?: Promise<void>;
75: 	#closed = false;
76: 
77: 	constructor(state: HindsightSessionState) {
78: 		this.#state = state;
79: 	}
80: 
81: 	get depth(): number {
82: 		return this.#items.length;
83: 	}
84: 
85: 	enqueue(content: string, context?: string): void {
86: 		if (this.#closed) {
87: 			throw new Error("Hindsight retain queue is closed.");
88: 		}
89: 		this.#items.push({ content, context, timestamp: new Date() });
90: 
91: 		if (this.#items.length >= RETAIN_FLUSH_BATCH_SIZE) {
92: 			void this.flush();
93: 			return;
94: 		}
95: 		if (!this.#timer) {
96: 			this.#timer = setTimeout(() => {
97: 				void this.flush();
98: 			}, RETAIN_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS);
99: 			// Don't pin the event loop alive just for a pending retain flush.
100: 			this.#timer.unref?.();
101: 		}
102: 	}
103: 
104: 	async flush(): Promise<void> {
105: 		if (this.#timer) {
106: 			clearTimeout(this.#timer);
107: 			this.#timer = undefined;
108: 		}
109: 
110: 		if (this.#flushing) {
111: 			// Coalesce: wait for the in-flight flush, then drain anything that
112: 			// landed after it started so we don't strand items.
113: 			await this.#flushing;
114: 			if (this.#items.length > 0) await this.flush();
115: 			return;
116: 		}
117: 
118: 		if (this.#items.length === 0) return;
119: 
120: 		const items = this.#items.splice(0);
121: 		const flushPromise = this.#doFlush(items);
122: 		this.#flushing = flushPromise;
123: 		try {
124: 			await flushPromise;
125: 		} finally {
126: 			this.#flushing = undefined;
127: 		}
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	dispose(): void {
131: 		this.#closed = true;
132: 		if (this.#timer) {
133: 			clearTimeout(this.#timer);
134: 			this.#timer = undefined;
135: 		}
136: 		this.#items = [];
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	async #doFlush(items: PendingRetainItem[]): Promise<void> {
140: 		const state = this.#state;
141: 		const sessionId = state.sessionId;
142: 		if (state.session.getHindsightSessionState() !== state) {
143: 			// Session went away before we could flush. We can't notify anyone, so
144: 			// log and drop — these are best-effort facts, not transactional writes.
145: 			logger.warn("Hindsight retain queue: session vanished, dropping batch", {
146: 				sessionId,
147: 				items: items.length,
148: 			});
149: 			return;
150: 		}
151: 
152: 		try {
153: 			await ensureBankExists(state.client, state.bankId, state.config, state.banksSet);
154: 			const batch: MemoryItemInput[] = items.map(item => ({
155: 				content: item.content,
156: 				context: item.context ?? state.config.retainContext,
157: 				metadata: { session_id: sessionId },
158: 				tags: state.retainTags,
159: 				timestamp: item.timestamp,
160: 			}));
161: 			await state.client.retainBatch(state.bankId, batch, { async: true });
162: 			if (state.config.debug) {
163: 				logger.debug("Hindsight retain queue: batch flushed", {
164: 					sessionId,
165: 					bankId: state.bankId,
166: 					items: items.length,
167: 				});
168: 			}
169: 		} catch (err) {
170: 			const errorText = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
171: 			logger.warn("Hindsight retain queue: batch flush failed", {
172: 				sessionId,
173: 				bankId: state.bankId,
174: 				items: items.length,
175: 				error: errorText,
176: 			});
177: 			this.#notifyRetainFailure(items.length, errorText);
178: 		}
179: 	}
180: 
181: 	#notifyRetainFailure(count: number, errorText: string): void {
182: 		const noun = count === 1 ? "memory" : "memories";
183: 		this.#state.session.emitNotice(
184: 			"warning",
185: 			`Memory retention failed for ${count} ${noun}: ${errorText}`,
186: 			"Hindsight",
187: 		);
188: 	}
189: }
190: 
191: /** Rolling hash of messages[0, count) for retention-cache validation (see #lastRetainedPrefixKey). */
192: function retentionPrefixKey(messages: HindsightMessage[], count: number): string {
193: 	let key = "";
194: 	for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
195: 		const m = messages[i];
196: 		if (m === undefined) break;
197: 		key = Bun.hash(`${key}\u0000${m.role}\u0000${m.content}\u0000${m.timestamp ?? ""}`).toString(36);
198: 	}
199: 	return key;
200: }
201: 
202: /** Per-session Hindsight runtime state owned by its AgentSession. */
203: export class HindsightSessionState {
204: 	/** Session id used for retain-queue metadata. */
205: 	sessionId: string;
206: 	client: HindsightApi;
207: 	bankId: string;
208: 	/** Tags applied to every retain — non-empty in per-project-tagged mode. */
209: 	retainTags?: string[];
210: 	/** Tag filter applied to every recall/reflect — non-empty in per-project-tagged mode. */
211: 	recallTags?: string[];
212: 	recallTagsMatch?: "any" | "all" | "any_strict" | "all_strict";
213: 	config: HindsightConfig;
214: 	session: AgentSession;
215: 	banksSet: Set<string>;
216: 	lastRetainedTurn: number;
217: 	#lastRetainedMessageIndex: number = 0;
218: 	#cachedTranscript: string = "";
219: 	// Rolling hash of ALL messages in [0, #lastRetainedMessageIndex) at cache
220: 	// time. The incremental full-session cache assumes the branch is append-only;
221: 	// a rewind, branch switch, compaction, or in-place edit rewrites the prefix
222: 	// without changing the session id. Re-hashing the current prefix at use time
223: 	// makes the cache self-healing: on ANY prefix change (not just the boundary
224: 	// message) we rebuild the full transcript instead of retaining stale content
225: 	// or silently retaining nothing forever. Hashing is orders of magnitude
226: 	// cheaper than the re-formatting this cache avoids.
227: 	#lastRetainedPrefixKey: string = "";
228: 	hasRecalledForFirstTurn: boolean;
229: 	lastRecallSnippet?: string;
230: 	#recallGeneration = 0;
231: 	/** Cached `<mental_models>` block injected into developer instructions. */
232: 	mentalModelsSnippet?: string;
233: 	/** When the current bootstrap/boundary load settled; gates the first-turn race. */
234: 	mentalModelsLoadedAt?: number;
235: 	/**
236: 	 * In-flight bootstrap or transcript-boundary load. `beforeAgentStartPrompt`
237: 	 * awaits it on the first turn so a timely snapshot lands before generation,
238: 	 * even though startup and transcript transitions remain non-blocking.
239: 	 */
240: 	mentalModelsLoadPromise?: Promise<void>;
241: 	#mentalModelsLoadGeneration = 0;
242: 	unsubscribe?: () => void;
243: 	/**
244: 	 * Releases the `onHindsightScopeChanged` subscription that drives live
245: 	 * rebuilds when `hindsight.bankId` / `bankIdPrefix` / `scoping` change.
246: 	 * Only set on primary states; aliases inherit the parent's subscription.
247: 	 */
248: 	unsubscribeScope?: () => void;
249: 	/** Alias states delegate persistence config to a primary parent state. */
250: 	aliasOf?: HindsightSessionState;
251: 	readonly retainQueue: HindsightRetainQueue;
252: 
253: 	constructor(options: HindsightSessionStateOptions) {
254: 		this.sessionId = options.sessionId;
255: 		this.client = options.client;
256: 		this.bankId = options.bankId;
257: 		this.retainTags = options.retainTags;
258: 		this.recallTags = options.recallTags;
259: 		this.recallTagsMatch = options.recallTagsMatch;
260: 		this.config = options.config;
261: 		this.session = options.session;
262: 		this.banksSet = options.banksSet;
263: 		this.lastRetainedTurn = options.lastRetainedTurn ?? 0;
264: 		this.#lastRetainedMessageIndex = 0;
265: 		this.#cachedTranscript = "";
266: 		this.#lastRetainedPrefixKey = "";
267: 		this.hasRecalledForFirstTurn = options.hasRecalledForFirstTurn ?? false;
268: 		this.aliasOf = options.aliasOf;
269: 		this.retainQueue = new HindsightRetainQueue(this);
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	setSessionId(sessionId: string): void {
273: 		if (this.sessionId !== sessionId) this.#recallGeneration++;
274: 		this.sessionId = sessionId;
275: 		this.#lastRetainedMessageIndex = 0;
276: 		this.#cachedTranscript = "";
277: 		this.#lastRetainedPrefixKey = "";
278: 	}
279: 
280: 	resetConversationTracking(): void {
281: 		this.#recallGeneration++;
282: 		this.lastRetainedTurn = 0;
283: 		this.hasRecalledForFirstTurn = false;
284: 		this.lastRecallSnippet = undefined;
285: 		this.#lastRetainedMessageIndex = 0;
286: 		this.#cachedTranscript = "";
287: 		this.#lastRetainedPrefixKey = "";
288: 	}
289: 
290: 	enqueueRetain(content: string, context?: string): void {
291: 		this.retainQueue.enqueue(content, context);
292: 	}
293: 
294: 	async flushRetainQueue(): Promise<void> {
295: 		await this.retainQueue.flush();
296: 	}
297: 
298: 	async recallForContext(query: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<RecallOutcome> {
299: 		try {
300: 			const response = await this.client.recall(this.bankId, query, {
301: 				budget: this.config.recallBudget,
302: 				maxTokens: this.config.recallMaxTokens,
303: 				types: this.config.recallTypes.length > 0 ? this.config.recallTypes : undefined,
304: 				tags: this.recallTags,
305: 				tagsMatch: this.recallTagsMatch,
306: 				signal,
307: 			});
308: 			if (signal?.aborted) return { context: null, ok: false };
309: 			const results = response.results ?? [];
310: 			if (results.length === 0) return { context: null, ok: true };
311: 			const formatted = formatMemories(results);
312: 			const block = `<memories>\n${this.config.recallPromptPreamble}\n\n${formatted}\n</memories>`;
313: 			return { context: block, ok: true };
314: 		} catch (err) {
315: 			if (this.config.debug) {
316: 				logger.debug("Hindsight: recall failed", { bankId: this.bankId, error: String(err) });
317: 			}
318: 			return { context: null, ok: false };
319: 		}
320: 	}
321: 
322: 	#sessionSourceTimestamp(): Date | undefined {
323: 		const header = this.session.sessionManager?.getHeader?.();
324: 		const timestamp = header?.timestamp;
325: 		if (typeof timestamp !== "string") return undefined;
326: 		const trimmed = timestamp.trim();
327: 		if (!trimmed) return undefined;
328: 		const parsed = new Date(trimmed);
329: 		return Number.isNaN(parsed.getTime()) ? undefined : parsed;
330: 	}
331: 
332: 	async retainSession(messages: HindsightMessage[]): Promise<void> {
333: 		const retainedAt = new Date();
334: 		const sourceTimestamp = this.#sessionSourceTimestamp() ?? retainedAt;
335: 		const retainFullWindow = this.config.retainMode === "full-session";
336: 		let documentId: string;
337: 		let transcript: string;
338: 		let nextCachedTranscript: string | undefined;
339: 
340: 		if (retainFullWindow) {
341: 			documentId = this.sessionId;
342: 			const boundary = this.#lastRetainedMessageIndex;
343: 			if (boundary > messages.length || retentionPrefixKey(messages, boundary) !== this.#lastRetainedPrefixKey) {
344: 				this.#lastRetainedMessageIndex = 0;
345: 				this.#cachedTranscript = "";
346: 				this.#lastRetainedPrefixKey = "";
347: 			}
348: 			const newMessages = messages.slice(this.#lastRetainedMessageIndex);
349: 			const { transcript: newPart } = prepareRetentionTranscript(newMessages, true, { includeTimestamps: true });
350: 			if (!newPart) return;
351: 			nextCachedTranscript = this.#cachedTranscript ? `${this.#cachedTranscript}\n\n${newPart}` : newPart;
352: 			transcript = nextCachedTranscript;
353: 		} else {
354: 			const windowTurns = this.config.retainEveryNTurns + this.config.retainOverlapTurns;
355: 			const target = sliceLastTurnsByUserBoundary(messages, windowTurns);
356: 			documentId = `${this.sessionId}-${retainedAt.getTime()}`;
357: 			this.#lastRetainedMessageIndex = 0;
358: 			this.#cachedTranscript = "";
359: 			this.#lastRetainedPrefixKey = "";
360: 			const { transcript: windowTranscript } = prepareRetentionTranscript(target, true, { includeTimestamps: true });
361: 			if (!windowTranscript) return;
362: 			transcript = windowTranscript;
363: 		}
364: 
365: 		await ensureBankExists(this.client, this.bankId, this.config, this.banksSet);
366: 		await this.client.retain(this.bankId, transcript, {
367: 			documentId,
368: 			context: this.config.retainContext,
369: 			metadata: { session_id: this.sessionId },
370: 			tags: this.retainTags,
371: 			timestamp: sourceTimestamp,
372: 			async: true,
373: 		});
374: 		if (nextCachedTranscript !== undefined) {
375: 			this.#cachedTranscript = nextCachedTranscript;
376: 			this.#lastRetainedMessageIndex = messages.length;
377: 			this.#lastRetainedPrefixKey = retentionPrefixKey(messages, messages.length);
378: 		}
379: 	}
380: 
381: 	async maybeRetainOnAgentEnd(): Promise<void> {
382: 		if (!this.config.autoRetain) return;
383: 		const messages = extractMessages(this.session.sessionManager);
384: 		if (messages.length === 0) return;
385: 		const userTurns = messages.filter(m => m.role === "user").length;
386: 		if (userTurns - this.lastRetainedTurn < this.config.retainEveryNTurns) return;
387: 
388: 		try {
389: 			await this.retainSession(messages);
390: 			this.lastRetainedTurn = userTurns;
391: 			if (this.config.debug) {
392: 				logger.debug("Hindsight: auto-retain succeeded", {
393: 					sessionId: this.sessionId,
394: 					bankId: this.bankId,
395: 					userTurns,
396: 					messages: messages.length,
397: 				});
398: 			}
399: 		} catch (err) {
400: 			logger.warn("Hindsight: auto-retain failed", {
401: 				sessionId: this.sessionId,
402: 				bankId: this.bankId,
403: 				error: String(err),
404: 			});
405: 		}
406: 	}
407: 
408: 	async forceRetainCurrentSession(): Promise<void> {
409: 		const messages = extractMessages(this.session.sessionManager);
410: 		if (messages.length === 0) return;
411: 		// Forced retains are user-initiated rebuilds (`/memory enqueue`): drop the
412: 		// incremental cache so the full transcript is reformatted and resent even
413: 		// when no new messages arrived since the last auto-retain — otherwise a
414: 		// rebuild could never recover an upstream document that was deleted or a
415: 		// previous async retain that never materialized.
416: 		this.#lastRetainedMessageIndex = 0;
417: 		this.#cachedTranscript = "";
418: 		this.#lastRetainedPrefixKey = "";
419: 		try {
420: 			await this.retainSession(messages);
421: 			this.lastRetainedTurn = messages.filter(m => m.role === "user").length;
422: 		} catch (err) {
423: 			logger.warn("Hindsight: forced retain failed", {
424: 				sessionId: this.sessionId,
425: 				bankId: this.bankId,
426: 				error: String(err),
427: 			});
428: 		}
429: 	}
430: 
431: 	async beforeAgentStartPrompt(
432: 		promptText: string,
433: 		signal?: AbortSignal,
434: 	): Promise<MemoryPromptPreparation | undefined> {
435: 		if (this.config.mentalModelsEnabled && this.mentalModelsLoadPromise && this.mentalModelsLoadedAt === undefined) {
436: 			await Promise.race([this.mentalModelsLoadPromise, Bun.sleep(MENTAL_MODEL_FIRST_TURN_DEADLINE_MS)]);
437: 		}
438: 
439: 		if (!this.config.autoRecall || this.hasRecalledForFirstTurn) return undefined;
440: 
441: 		const latestPrompt = promptText.trim();
442: 		if (!latestPrompt) return undefined;
443: 		const generation = ++this.#recallGeneration;
444: 
445: 		const history = extractMessages(this.session.sessionManager);
446: 		const queryMessages = [...history, { role: "user" as const, content: latestPrompt }];
447: 		const query = composeRecallQuery(latestPrompt, queryMessages, this.config.recallContextTurns);
448: 		const truncated = truncateRecallQuery(query, latestPrompt, this.config.recallMaxQueryChars);
449: 		const { context, ok } = await this.recallForContext(truncated, signal);
450: 		if (!ok) return undefined;
451: 
452: 		return {
453: 			context: context ?? undefined,
454: 			commit: () => {
455: 				if (this.#recallGeneration !== generation) return false;
456: 				this.hasRecalledForFirstTurn = true;
457: 				if (context) this.lastRecallSnippet = context;
458: 				return true;
459: 			},
460: 		};
461: 	}
462: 
463: 	async recallForCompaction(messages: HindsightMessage[]): Promise<string | undefined> {
464: 		const lastUser = messages.findLast(m => m.role === "user");
465: 		if (!lastUser) return undefined;
466: 
467: 		const query = composeRecallQuery(lastUser.content, messages, this.config.recallContextTurns);
468: 		const truncated = truncateRecallQuery(query, lastUser.content, this.config.recallMaxQueryChars);
469: 		const { context } = await this.recallForContext(truncated);
470: 		return context ?? undefined;
471: 	}
472: 
473: 	async runMentalModelLoad(scope: BankScope): Promise<void> {
474: 		if (!this.config.mentalModelsEnabled) return;
475: 		const generation = ++this.#mentalModelsLoadGeneration;
476: 		const previousSnippet = this.mentalModelsSnippet;
477: 		this.mentalModelsLoadedAt = undefined;
478: 
479: 		const bootstrap = (async () => {
480: 			// Create/ensure the bank BEFORE the first mental-model POST so we don't
481: 			// land `createMentalModel` against a bank the server has never seen —
482: 			// that surfaces as a FK / 404 on Hindsight's side. `ensureBankExists`
483: 			// is idempotent (PUT) and skips after the first call via `banksSet`.
484: 			await ensureBankExists(this.client, this.bankId, this.config, this.banksSet);
485: 
486: 			// Seeding is opt-in (`hindsight.mentalModelAutoSeed`). Default behaviour is
487: 			// read-only: we surface whatever models the operator has curated on the
488: 			// bank, but we do NOT POST to create new ones unless they explicitly
489: 			// asked. `/memory mm seed` remains the explicit-write entry point.
490: 			if (this.config.mentalModelAutoSeed) {
491: 				const seeds = resolveSeedsForScope(scope, this.config.scoping);
492: 				if (seeds.length > 0) {
493: 					await ensureMentalModels(this.client, this.bankId, seeds, this.config.debug);
494: 				}
495: 			}
496: 
497: 			await this.#loadAndPublishMentalModels(generation, previousSnippet, "MM load");
498: 		})();
499: 		await this.#settleMentalModelsLoadWithinDeadline(bootstrap, generation, previousSnippet);
500: 	}
501: 
502: 	/**
503: 	 * Starts a bounded reload for a new transcript without blocking the session
504: 	 * transition. A result that misses the first-turn deadline is discarded so
505: 	 * the previous snapshot stays frozen for the whole transcript.
506: 	 */
507: 	beginMentalModelsTranscriptReload(): void {
508: 		if (!this.config.mentalModelsEnabled) return;
509: 		const generation = ++this.#mentalModelsLoadGeneration;
510: 		const previousSnippet = this.mentalModelsSnippet;
511: 		this.mentalModelsLoadedAt = undefined;
512: 		const reload = this.#settleMentalModelsLoadWithinDeadline(
513: 			this.#loadAndPublishMentalModels(generation, previousSnippet, "MM transcript reload"),
514: 			generation,
515: 			previousSnippet,
516: 		).catch(error => {
517: 			if (generation === this.#mentalModelsLoadGeneration) {
518: 				this.mentalModelsSnippet = previousSnippet;
519: 				this.mentalModelsLoadedAt = Date.now();
520: 			}
521: 			logger.debug("Hindsight: mental-model transcript reload failed", { error: String(error) });
522: 		});
523: 		this.mentalModelsLoadPromise = reload;
524: 	}
525: 
526: 	async #settleMentalModelsLoadWithinDeadline(
527: 		load: Promise<void>,
528: 		generation: number,
529: 		previousSnippet: string | undefined,
530: 	): Promise<void> {
531: 		const outcome = await Promise.race([
532: 			load,
533: 			Bun.sleep(MENTAL_MODEL_FIRST_TURN_DEADLINE_MS).then(() => MENTAL_MODEL_LOAD_TIMED_OUT),
534: 		]);
535: 		if (outcome !== MENTAL_MODEL_LOAD_TIMED_OUT || generation !== this.#mentalModelsLoadGeneration) return;
536: 
537: 		// Invalidate the still-running load before restoring the stable snapshot.
538: 		// SessionTools checks the same generation before committing a prompt build,
539: 		// so a queued publication cannot rewrite the prefix after this deadline.
540: 		this.#mentalModelsLoadGeneration++;
541: 		this.mentalModelsSnippet = previousSnippet;
542: 		this.mentalModelsLoadedAt = Date.now();
543: 	}
544: 
545: 	async #loadAndPublishMentalModels(
546: 		generation: number,
547: 		previousSnippet: string | undefined,
548: 		reason: "MM load" | "MM reload" | "MM transcript reload",
549: 	): Promise<void> {
550: 		const result = await tryLoadMentalModelsBlock(
551: 			this.client,
552: 			this.bankId,
553: 			this.config.mentalModelMaxRenderChars,
554: 			this.recallTags,
555: 		);
556: 		if (generation !== this.#mentalModelsLoadGeneration) return;
557: 		if (!result.ok) {
558: 			this.mentalModelsLoadedAt = Date.now();
559: 			return;
560: 		}
561: 
562: 		this.mentalModelsSnippet = result.block;
563: 		const published = await this.#refreshBaseSystemPromptAfter(
564: 			reason,
565: 			() => generation === this.#mentalModelsLoadGeneration,
566: 		);
567: 		if (generation !== this.#mentalModelsLoadGeneration) return;
568: 		if (!published) this.mentalModelsSnippet = previousSnippet;
569: 		this.mentalModelsLoadedAt = Date.now();
570: 	}
571: 
572: 	async reloadMentalModels(): Promise<boolean> {
573: 		if (this.aliasOf) return false;
574: 		if (!this.config.mentalModelsEnabled) return false;
575: 		const generation = ++this.#mentalModelsLoadGeneration;

# Kappa CLI package guidelines

## Build/Test

- **Run**: `bun run --conditions=browser ./src/index.ts`
- **Test**: `bun test` (all tests) or `bun test test/tool/tool.test.ts` (single test)
- **Typecheck**: `bun run typecheck` (runs `tsgo --noEmit`)

## Import Aliases

- `@/*` maps to `./src/*`
- `@tui/*` maps to `./src/cli/cmd/tui/*`

## Key Patterns

**Namespace modules** -- Code is organized as TypeScript namespaces, not classes. Each module exports a namespace with its Zod schemas, types, and functions:

```ts
export namespace Session {
  export const Info = z.object({ ... })
  export type Info = z.infer<typeof Info>
  export const create = fn(z.object({ ... }), async (input) => { ... })
}
```

**`Instance.state(init, dispose?)`** -- Per-project lazy singleton. Many modules register state this way. The state is tied to the project directory via `AsyncLocalStorage`:

```ts
const state = Instance.state(async () => {
  // initialized once per project, cached
  return { ... }
})
// later: (await state()).someValue
```

**Service-closure state vs. directory state** -- A value created in a service-layer closure, outside `InstanceState`, is shared by that service instance rather than keyed by request directory. The shared VS Code session paths use one active Snapshot service for the sidebar, Kappa tabs, and Agent Manager local worktree requests, so Snapshot `trackState` and its slow-track `asked` guard span those directories. Choosing **Continue with snapshots** resets the guard only when continued tracking returns a snapshot hash.

**`fn(schema, callback)`** -- Wraps functions with Zod input validation. Used for most exported functions:

```ts
export const get = fn(z.object({ id: z.string() }), async (input) => { ... })
```

**`Tool.define(id, init)`** -- All tools follow this pattern. The `init` returns `{ description, parameters, execute }`. Output is auto-truncated.

**`BusEvent.define(type, schema)` + `Bus.publish()`** -- In-process pub/sub event system for cross-module communication.

**`NamedError.create(name, schema)`** -- Structured errors with Zod schemas. Prefer these over throwing raw errors.

**`iife()`** -- Immediately-invoked function expression helper. Used to avoid `let` statements per style guide.

**Logging** -- Use `Log.create({ service: "name" })` pattern.

## Process Spawning (Windows)

On Windows, any `spawn`/`execFile` call without `windowsHide: true` will flash a cmd.exe console window at the user. Use `Process.spawn` from `src/util/process.ts` — it enforces `windowsHide: true` automatically. For `Bun.spawn`/`Bun.spawnSync`, pass `windowsHide` via the options object if the subprocess could create a visible console.

The MCP `StdioClientTransport` (third-party SDK) is handled separately via a process shim in `src/mcp/index.ts` that sets `process.type = "browser"` when running inside the VS Code extension (`KAPPA_PLATFORM=vscode`), which causes the SDK's internal `isElectron()` check to return `true` and enable `windowsHide`.

## Storage

Filesystem-based JSON, not a database. Data lives in `~/.local/share/kappa/storage/`. Keys are path arrays: `Storage.write(["session", projectID, sessionID], data)`.

## TUI

Built with **SolidJS + OpenTUI** (`@opentui/solid`) -- a terminal UI framework. JSX renders to the terminal using elements like `<box>`, `<text>`, `<scrollbox>`. The TUI communicates with the server via `@kappacode/sdk`.

## Server

Hono-based HTTP server with OpenAPI spec generation. SSE for real-time events. When you add/change routes, regenerate the SDK (see root AGENTS.md for the command).

## Providers and Models

Uses the **Vercel AI SDK** as the abstraction layer. Providers are loaded from a bundled map or dynamically installed at runtime. Models come from models.dev (external API), cached locally.

## Fork Isolation Rule

`opencode/` is a fork of upstream opencode. When a change must touch a shared upstream file, extract the Kappa-specific logic into a mirror file under `src/kappacode/<same/path>.ts` (tests under `test/kappacode/<same/path>.test.ts`) and call into it from the upstream file behind a single `kappacode_change` marker. Example: a Kappa override for `src/cli/cmd/tui/component/dialog-provider.tsx` lives at `src/kappacode/cli/cmd/tui/component/dialog-provider.tsx`. Avoid inlining Kappa-specific logic directly into shared upstream files. Files and directories whose path contains `kappacode` never need `kappacode_change` markers.

</system-reminder>

136:   function clip(input: string, max: number): string {

142:   function catalog(memory: MemoryService.Interface, input: { root: string; query: string }) {
143:     const filter = input.query.toLowerCase()
144:     return Effect.gen(function* () {
145:       const lines: string[] = []
146:       const files: string[] = []
147:       let count = 0
148:       for (const file of MemorySchema.Sources) {
149:         const text = yield* memory.readSource({ root: input.root, file })
150:         const rows: string[] = []
151:         for (const raw of text.split("\n")) {
152:           const line = raw.trim()
153:           if (line.startsWith("## ")) continue
154:           const idx = line.indexOf(" :: ")
155:           if (!line.startsWith("- ") || idx < 0) continue
156:           const key = line.slice(2, idx).trim()
157:           const value = line.slice(idx + 4).trim()
158:           if (!key || !value) continue
159:           if (filter && !`${key} ${value}`.toLowerCase().includes(filter)) continue
160:           rows.push(`- ${key} :: ${value.length > 60 ? `${value.slice(0, 57)}...` : value}`)
161:         }
162:         if (rows.length === 0) continue
163:         files.push(file)
164:         lines.push(`## ${file}`, ...rows)
165:         count += rows.length
166:       }
167:       const sessions = yield* memory.recent({
168:         root: input.root,
169:         limit: CATALOG_SESSION_LIMIT,
170:         max: CATALOG_SESSION_SUMMARY,
171:       })
172:       const sessionRows: string[] = []
173:       for (const item of sessions) {
174:         if (filter && !`${item.id} ${item.topic} ${item.summary}`.toLowerCase().includes(filter)) continue
175:         const date = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/.exec(item.time)?.[0] ?? ""
176:         sessionRows.push(
177:           `- session=${item.id}${[item.topic, date]
178:             .filter(Boolean)
179:             .map((part) => ` ${part}`)
180:             .join("")}`,
181:         )
182:       }
183:       if (sessionRows.length > 0) {
184:         lines.push(`## sessions`, ...sessionRows)
185:         count += sessionRows.length
186:       }
187:       const head = `# Kappa Memory Catalog (${count} entr${count === 1 ? "y" : "ies"}${filter ? `, filter "${input.query}"` : ""})`
188:       const body = [head, ...lines].join("\n")
189:       const output =
190:         Buffer.byteLength(body) > CATALOG_MAX_BYTES
191:           ? `${clip(body, CATALOG_MAX_BYTES)}\n[truncated: refine with a query filter]`
192:           : body
193:       return { output: count ? output : "No stored memory entries matched.", count, files }
194:     })
195:   }

213:       const safe = { ...result, output: block(result.output) }
214:       yield* input.memory.recordRecall({ root: live.root, sessionID: live.current, now: Date.now(), count: result.count })
215:       return {
216:         title: `Kappa memory catalog: ${result.count} entr${result.count === 1 ? "y" : "ies"}`,
217:         output: safe.output,

219:       } satisfies Result
220:     })

236:       const result = yield* input.memory.search({

247:       yield* input.memory.recordRecall({ root: live.root, sessionID: live.current, now: Date.now(), count: hits.length })
248: 
249:       if (hits.length === 0) {
250:         return {

252:           output,

255:       }
256: 
257:       return {

259:         output,

261:       } satisfies Result
262:     })

265:   export function recall(input: Recall) {
266:     return Effect.gen(function* () {
267:       const current = input.sessionID

269:       const state = yield* input.memory.state({ root })

274:       const query = input.params.query?.trim() ?? ""
275:       const mode = input.params.mode
276:       if (mode === "catalog") return yield* recallCatalog(input, live, query)
277:       if (input.params.mode !== "digest" && !query) return yield* recallQuery(input, live)
278:       return yield* recallSearch(input, live, query, mode)

355:   function forget(input: Save, root: string) {
356:     return Effect.gen(function* () {
357:       const query = (input.params.query ?? input.params.text ?? "").trim()
358:       if (!query) return noQuery()
359:       yield* approval(input.params, input.ask, { query })
360:       return removed({
361:         params: input.params,
362:         result: yield* input.memory.forget({ root, sessionID: input.sessionID, query }),
363:       })
364:     })
365:   }
366: 
367:   function write(input: Save, root: string) {
368:     return Effect.gen(function* () {
369:       const text = (input.params.text ?? "").trim()
370:       if (!text) return noText(input.params.action)
371: 
372:       yield* approval(input.params, input.ask, { text })
373:       const result =
374:         input.params.action === "correct"
375:           ? yield* input.memory.correct({ root, sessionID: input.sessionID, key: input.params.key, text })
376:           : yield* input.memory.remember({ root, sessionID: input.sessionID, key: input.params.key, text })
377:       return saved({ params: input.params, result })
378:     })
379:   }

381:   export function save(input: Save) {
382:     return Effect.gen(function* () {
383:       const root = yield* input.memory.prepare({ ctx: input.ctx })
384:       const state = yield* input.memory.state({ root })
385:       if (!state.enabled) return disabled()
386:       if (input.params.action === "forget") return yield* forget(input, root)
387:       if (input.params.action === "skip") return yield* skip(input)
388:       return yield* write(input, root)
389:     })

394:     if (action === "correct") return ["corrections.md"]

396:     return ["project.md"]

400:     if (input.action === "skip") return "Kappa memory skipped: out of scope"
401:     if (input.action === "forget") return `Kappa memory updated: ${input.removed} removed`
402:     if (input.added === 0) return "Kappa memory unchanged"
403:     if (input.action === "correct")
404:       return `Kappa memory correction saved: ${input.added} op${input.added === 1 ? "" : "s"}`
405:     return `Kappa memory saved: ${input.added} op${input.added === 1 ? "" : "s"}`
406:   }

411:     added: number

418:       `added=${input.added}`,

390:   /** Drop the cached enabled flag for a root so the next probe re-reads fresh state.

396:   /** Per-turn cache of `KappaMemory.toolEnabled` keyed by root string, with a short TTL so the
397:    * step-loop coalesces probes inside a single turn. Cache is invalidated immediately on enable /
398:    * disable / purge / rebuild via the MemoryEvents bus (subscribed in kappacode/bootstrap.ts). */
399:   export function memoryToolsEnabled(input: { ctx: MemoryPaths.Ctx }) {
400:     return Effect.gen(function* () {
401:       const root = MemoryPaths.root({ ctx: input.ctx })
402:       const cached = memoryEnabledCache.get(root)
403:       if (cached && cached.deadline > Date.now()) return cached.enabled
404:       const enabled = yield* Effect.tryPromise({
405:         try: () => KappaMemory.toolEnabled({ ctx: input.ctx }),
406:         catch: (err) => err,
407:       }).pipe(
408:         Effect.catch((err) =>
409:           Effect.sync(() => {
410:             log.warn("memory tools unavailable", { error: String(err) })
411:             return false
412:           }),
413:         ),
414:       )
415:       memoryEnabledCache.set(root, { enabled, deadline: Date.now() + MEMORY_ENABLED_TTL_MS })
416:       if (memoryEnabledCache.size > MEMORY_ENABLED_CACHE_MAX) {
417:         const oldest = memoryEnabledCache.keys().next().value
418:         if (oldest !== undefined) memoryEnabledCache.delete(oldest)
419:       }
420:       return enabled
421:     })
422:   }

432:           return yield* Network.available(new URL(base), token)

441:       if (tool.id === "browser_open") return browser ? [tool] : []
442:       if (semantic) return [tool]
443:       if (tool.id === "semantic_search") return []
444:       if (tool.id !== "glob" && tool.id !== "grep") return [tool]
445:       const next = { ...tool, description: tool.description.replace(`\n${hint}`, "") }

312: // LPT to pack shards evenly; fewer, bigger batches set a floor under the slowest shard.
313: const KAPPACODE_ROOT_TIERS = 8
314: const kappacodeRootTier = (file: string) => {
315:   if (!file.startsWith("kappacode/")) return undefined
316:   if (file.slice("kappacode/".length).includes("/")) return undefined
317:   let hash = 0
318:   for (let i = 0; i < file.length; i++) hash = (hash * 31 + file.charCodeAt(i)) | 0
319:   return `fast-tier-kappacode-root-${Math.abs(hash) % KAPPACODE_ROOT_TIERS}`
320: }
321: const tierOf = (file: string) => {
322:   if (isBatchExcluded(file)) return undefined
323:   for (const [name, entries] of Object.entries(FAST_TIERS)) {
324:     if (entries.some((entry) => matchesEntry(file, entry))) return name
325:   }
326:   return kappacodeRootTier(file)
327: }
328: const batches = new Map<string, string[]>()
329: // --update-durations disables batching so every file runs (and is measured) individually;
330: // batched members otherwise never appear in results and their entries would rot.
331: if (patterns.length === 0 && !profile && !updateDurations) {
332:   for (const file of candidates) {
333:     const tier = tierOf(file)
334:     if (!tier) continue
335:     const members = batches.get(tier) ?? []
336:     members.push(file)
337:     batches.set(tier, members)
338:   }
339: 
340:   // A batch shares one process, so process-wide mutations poison every later file in it.
341:   // Scan member sources for the known-unsafe markers and demote matches to per-file runs:
342:   // bun's mock.module is process-wide and permanent, AppRuntime.dispose() kills the shared
343:   // runtime, and global-fetch spies observe batch-mates' traffic. A developer adding such
344:   // a test anywhere keeps a green suite; the file just does not share a process.
345:   // Limitation: only the test file's own source is scanned — a marker hidden in an
346:   // imported helper is invisible; batch-only failures that vanish per-file point there.
347:   // Markers: bun module mocks, disposal of the shared app runtime, spies on true globals,
348:   // and module-scope env writes (column 0 — env set inside a test body is indented and
349:   // typically restored; a load-time write leaks into every batch-mate's import snapshot).
350:   const unsafe = [
351:     /\bmock\.module\s*\(/,
352:     /\bAppRuntime\.dispose\s*\(/,
353:     /\bspyOn\s*\(\s*globalThis\b/,
354:     /^process\.env[.[]/m,
355:   ]
356:   const demoted = new Set<string>()
357:   const members = [...batches.values()].flat()
358:   // Bounded chunks: an unbounded Promise.all over ~440 files can exhaust low soft
359:   // fd limits (macOS shells commonly default to 256) before a single test runs.
360:   for (let i = 0; i < members.length; i += 64) {
361:     await Promise.all(
362:       members.slice(i, i + 64).map(async (member) => {
363:         const source = await Bun.file(path.join(root, "test", member)).text()
364:         if (unsafe.some((pattern) => pattern.test(source))) demoted.add(member)
365:       }),
366:     )
367:   }
368:   if (demoted.size > 0) {
369:     console.log(
370:       `Fast tier: ${demoted.size} file(s) use process-wide mocks/disposal/spies and run per-file instead:\n` +
371:         [...demoted].map((file) => `- ${file}`).join("\n"),
372:     )
373:     for (const [name, members] of batches)
374:       batches.set(
375:         name,
376:         members.filter((member) => !demoted.has(member)),
377:       )
378:   }
379:   for (const [name, members] of batches) if (members.length < 2) batches.delete(name)
380: }
381: const batched = new Set([...batches.values()].flat())
382: const shardInput = [...batches.keys(), ...candidates.filter((file) => !batched.has(file))]
383: // A batch runs its members sequentially, so its weight is the sum of member durations
384: // (hint > measured > a typical boot-dominated file) plus one process boot. Computed, not
385: // hand-maintained: stale per-tier constants systematically under-weighted heavy batches.
386: const TYPICAL_BATCHED_FILE_MS = 1_500
387: const BATCH_BOOT_MS = 3_000
388: const batchWeights = new Map(
389:   [...batches.entries()].map(([name, members]) => [
390:     name,
391:     members.reduce(
392:       (total, member) => total + (DURATION_HINTS[member] ?? measuredDurations[member] ?? TYPICAL_BATCHED_FILE_MS),
393:       BATCH_BOOT_MS,
394:     ),
395:   ]),
396: )
397: const shardWeight = (file: string) => batchWeights.get(file) ?? weight(file)
398: const files = shard ? TestShard.split(shardInput, shardWeight, shard.total)[shard.index - 1] : shardInput
399: // kappacode_change end
400: 
401: if (files.length === 0) {
402:   console.log("No test files found")
403:   process.exit(0)
404: }

406: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
407: // Types
408: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
409: 
410: type Result = {
411:   file: string
412:   passed: boolean
413:   code: number
414:   stdout: string
415:   stderr: string
416:   duration: number
417:   timedout: boolean
418:   deadline: number // kappacode_change - the kill deadline actually applied (batches get a roomier one)
419:   attempts: number
420: }
421: 
422: type Proc = ReturnType<typeof Bun.spawn>
423: 
424: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
425: // Setup
426: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
427: 
428: const xmldir = ci ? path.join(os.tmpdir(), `opencode-junit-${process.pid}`) : ""
429: if (ci) await fs.mkdir(xmldir, { recursive: true })
430: // kappacode_change start
431: const supplied = process.env[TestCli.ENV]
432: const built = supplied ? { binary: supplied, dir: undefined } : { binary: await TestCli.build(root), dir: undefined }
433: 
434: async function cleanBinary() {
435:   if (!built.dir) return
436:   await fs.rm(built.dir, { recursive: true, force: true })
437: }
438: // kappacode_change end
439: 
440: const counter = { done: 0 }
441: const pad = String(files.length).length
442: const progress = { width: 80 }
443: const active = new Map<number, ReturnType<typeof Bun.spawn>>()
444: const pending = new Map<number, Promise<void>>()
445: const stopping = { promise: undefined as Promise<void> | undefined }
446: const stopped = { value: false }
447: const marks = {
448:   pass: ".",
449:   retry: "R",
450:   fail: "F",
451:   timeout: "T",
452: } as const
453: const legend = `Legend: ${marks.pass}=pass ${marks.retry}=pass-after-retry ${marks.fail}=fail ${marks.timeout}=timeout`
454: 
455: function drain(stream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>) {
456:   const reader = stream.getReader()
457:   const decoder = new TextDecoder()
458:   const promise = (async () => {
459:     let text = ""
460:     while (true) {
461:       const chunk = await reader.read()
462:       if (chunk.done) return text + decoder.decode()
463:       text += decoder.decode(chunk.value, { stream: true })
464:     }
465:   })()
466:   return {
467:     promise,
468:     close: () => reader.cancel().catch(() => undefined),
469:   }
470: }
471: 
472: async function signal(proc: Proc, sig: "SIGTERM" | "SIGKILL") {
473:   if (process.platform === "win32") {
474:     const args = ["/pid", String(proc.pid), "/T"]
475:     if (sig === "SIGKILL") args.push("/F")
476:     const kill = Bun.spawn(["taskkill", ...args], {
477:       stdout: "ignore",
478:       stderr: "ignore",
479:       windowsHide: true,
480:     })
481:     await kill.exited
482:     return
483:   }
484: 
485:   const tree = Bun.spawn(["ps", "-axo", "pid=,ppid="], {
486:     stdout: "pipe",
487:     stderr: "ignore",
488:   })
489:   const [code, text] = await Promise.all([tree.exited, new Response(tree.stdout).text()])
490:   const rows = code === 0 ? text.trim().split("\n") : []
491:   const children = new Map<number, number[]>()
492:   for (const row of rows) {
493:     const [pid, parent] = row.trim().split(/\s+/).map(Number)
494:     if (!Number.isSafeInteger(pid) || !Number.isSafeInteger(parent)) continue
495:     const list = children.get(parent) ?? []
496:     list.push(pid)
497:     children.set(parent, list)
498:   }
499:   const collect = (pid: number): number[] => (children.get(pid) ?? []).flatMap((child) => [...collect(child), child])
500:   for (const pid of [...collect(proc.pid), proc.pid]) {
501:     for (const target of [-pid, pid]) {
502:       try {
503:         process.kill(target, sig)
504:       } catch (error) {
505:         if (typeof error === "object" && error !== null && "code" in error && error.code === "ESRCH") continue
506:         // A kill failure (e.g. EPERM in a sandboxed runner) must not take down the whole run.
507:         console.error(`warn: failed to signal ${target} with ${sig}:`, error)
508:       }
509:     }
510:   }
511: }
512: 
513: async function terminate(proc: Proc) {
514:   if (proc.exitCode !== null) return
515:   await signal(proc, "SIGTERM")
516:   const exited = Symbol("exited")
517:   const result = await Promise.race([proc.exited.then(() => exited), Bun.sleep(2_000)])
518:   if (result === exited) return
519:   await signal(proc, "SIGKILL")
520:   await Promise.race([proc.exited, Bun.sleep(2_000)])
521: }
522: 
523: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
524: // Run a single test file
525: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
526: 
527: async function run(file: string): Promise<Result> {
528:   // kappacode_change start - a fast-tier pseudo-file expands to all of its batch members in
529:   // one process; a shared pass compiles once, so it gets a roomier process deadline than a
530:   // single file even though each member is individually fast.
531:   const members = batches.get(file)
532:   const targets = members ? members.map((member) => path.join("test", member)) : [path.join("test", file)]
533:   const cmd = ["bun", "test", ...targets, "--timeout", String(timeout)]
534:   // kappacode_change end
535: 
536:   if (ci) {
537:     const name = file.replace(/[/\\]/g, "_") + ".xml"
538:     cmd.push("--reporter=junit", `--reporter-outfile=${path.join(xmldir, name)}`)
539:   }
540: 
541:   const start = performance.now()
542:   const killed = { value: false }
543:   const fileDeadline = members ? Math.max(deadline, 600_000) : deadline // kappacode_change
544: 
545:   const proc = Bun.spawn(cmd, {
546:     cwd: root,
547:     env: { ...process.env, [TestCli.ENV]: built.binary },
548:     stdout: "pipe",
549:     stderr: "pipe",
550:     windowsHide: true,
551:     detached: process.platform !== "win32",
552:   })
553:   active.set(proc.pid, proc)
554: 
555:   const stdout = drain(proc.stdout)
556:   const stderr = drain(proc.stderr)
557:   const code = await Promise.race([
558:     proc.exited.then((value) => ({ timedout: false, value })),
559:     Bun.sleep(fileDeadline).then(() => ({ timedout: true, value: -1 })), // kappacode_change
560:   ]).then(async (result) => {
561:     if (result.timedout) {
562:       killed.value = true
563:       await terminate(proc)
564:     }
565:     await finish(proc)
566:     return result.timedout ? (proc.exitCode ?? result.value) : result.value
567:   })
568:   const output = await Promise.race([
569:     Promise.all([stdout.promise, stderr.promise]).then((value) => ({ closed: true, value })),
570:     Bun.sleep(2_000).then(() => ({ closed: false, value: ["", ""] as [string, string] })),
571:   ]).then(async (result) => {
572:     if (result.closed) return result.value
573:     await signal(proc, "SIGKILL")
574:     await Promise.all([stdout.close(), stderr.close()])
575:     return Promise.all([stdout.promise, stderr.promise])
576:   })
577: 
578:   return {
579:     file,
580:     passed: code === 0,
581:     code,
582:     stdout: output[0],
583:     stderr: output[1],
584:     duration: performance.now() - start,
585:     timedout: killed.value,
586:     deadline: fileDeadline, // kappacode_change
587:     attempts: 1,
588:   }
589: }
590: 
591: function finish(proc: ReturnType<typeof Bun.spawn>) {
592:   const found = pending.get(proc.pid)
593:   if (found) return found
594: 
595:   const promise = (async () => {
596:     await Promise.race([proc.exited, Bun.sleep(2_000)])
597:     await cleanup(proc.pid)
598:   })().finally(() => {
599:     active.delete(proc.pid)
600:     pending.delete(proc.pid)
601:   })
602:   pending.set(proc.pid, promise)
603:   return promise
604: }
605: 
606: function shutdown(code: number) {
607:   if (stopping.promise) return stopping.promise
608:   stopping.promise = (async () => {
609:     stopped.value = true
610:     const children = [...active.values()]
611:     await Promise.all(children.map(terminate))
612:     await Promise.all(children.map(finish))
613:     await cleanBinary()
614:     process.exit(code)
615:   })()
616:   return stopping.promise
617: }
618: 
619: process.once("SIGINT", () => void shutdown(130))
620: process.once("SIGTERM", () => void shutdown(143))

622: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
623: // Report a single result
624: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
625: 
626: function mark(result: Result) {
627:   if (result.timedout) return marks.timeout
628:   if (!result.passed) return marks.fail
629:   if (result.attempts > 1) return marks.retry
630:   return marks.pass
631: }
632: 
633: function report(result: Result) {
634:   counter.done++
635:   if (dots) {
636:     process.stdout.write(mark(result))
637:     if (counter.done % progress.width === 0) process.stdout.write("\n")
638:     return
639:   }
640: 
641:   const idx = String(counter.done).padStart(pad)
642:   const secs = (result.duration / 1000).toFixed(1)
643:   const tries = result.attempts > 1 ? dim(` [attempt ${result.attempts}/${retries + 1}]`) : ""
644: 
645:   if (result.timedout) {
646:     console.log(
647:       `[${idx}/${files.length}] ${red("TIME")} ${result.file} ${dim(`(${secs}s - exceeded ${result.deadline / 1000}s)`)}${tries}`,
648:     )
649:     return
650:   }
651: 
652:   if (!result.passed) {
653:     console.log(`[${idx}/${files.length}] ${red("FAIL")} ${result.file} ${dim(`(${secs}s)`)}${tries}`)
654:     if (verbose && result.stderr.trim()) console.log(result.stderr)
655:     if (verbose && result.stdout.trim()) console.log(result.stdout)
656:     return
657:   }
658: 
659:   if (result.attempts > 1) {
660:     console.log(`[${idx}/${files.length}] ${yellow("FLAKY")} ${result.file} ${dim(`(${secs}s)`)}${tries}`)
661:     if (verbose && result.stdout.trim()) console.log(dim(result.stdout))
662:     return
663:   }
664: 
665:   console.log(`[${idx}/${files.length}] ${green("PASS")} ${result.file} ${dim(`(${secs}s)`)}`)
666:   if (verbose && result.stdout.trim()) console.log(dim(result.stdout))
667: }
668: 
669: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
670: // Parallel execution
671: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
672: 
673: // kappacode_change start - report the batches so shard logs stay interpretable
674: for (const [name, members] of batches) {
675:   if (!files.includes(name)) continue
676:   console.log(`\nFast tier ${bold(name)}: ${bold(String(members.length))} isolation-safe files in one shared process`)
677: }
678: // kappacode_change end
679: console.log(`\nRunning ${bold(String(files.length))} test files with concurrency ${bold(String(concurrency))}`)
680: if (shard) console.log(`Using balanced test shard ${shard.index}/${shard.total}`)
681: if (dots) console.log(dim(legend))
682: console.log()
